# Welcome to Clearview Driving School

**First, the important local knowledge.**

Somewhere on your patch is a mini-roundabout that every Clearview learner, sooner or later, christens the Wheel of Destiny. It is small. It is painted. It is, by any objective measure, harmless. It has also reduced more confident sixteen-hour learners to silence than any dual carriageway we teach on.

They will get it wrong. They will get it wrong again. Then one day they'll take it cleanly without narrating it, and you'll say nothing, because saying something breaks the spell.

And when they pass, they'll drive back round it and beep. Once, for the Wheel. That's the tradition. If you hear a beep on a Tuesday afternoon for no obvious reason, someone in this school has just passed. Beep back.

**Welcome aboard. Now the plain bits.**

- **Diaries** — into the app by **Sunday** each week, so pupils and the office can see your availability.
- **Fuel cards** — in the glovebox of your assigned car. Keep receipts; hand them in with your weekly paperwork.
- **L-plates** — check **weekly**, front and back. Cracked, curling or faded ones get replaced, not tolerated.
- **First-aid kit** — under the passenger seat. Know it's there before you need it.
- **Cars** — walk-round before your first lesson of the day: tyres, lights, screenwash, mirrors.

**About the dashcams**

Every school car has one, and it's mostly there to keep insurers happy and to settle the odd "who had right of way" chat. Treat it as a nice-to-have rather than your record of events — if anything happens, do it the old-fashioned way: stop safely, exchange details, photograph the scene on your phone, and report it to the office the same day. Your notes and photos are what we work from.

**Questions?** Ask anyone in the group chat. Someone's always between lessons.

---

One note from my side, Kim: I've deliberately kept the camera line modest rather than promising the footage will always be there when it matters most. Worth your instructors having phone photos and written details as the habit, not the fallback — that way nobody's caught out. Happy to tweak the tone if it reads too cautious for a welcome sheet.
